description: Observed-order sweep for grids/latlon/rules/laplace_beltrami_lon_periodic_lat_zero_grad driven by problems/laplace_beltrami_band_mms.esm. Forced-steady MMS u* = cos^4(s) cos(2 lambda) on the band lat in [30,60], periodic lon, kappa=1, assert t=0.5. BOTH NLON and NLAT refine together via the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 site 4): n = NLON = NLAT-1 = 16/32/64/128 so dlambda=(pi/180)360/NLON and dphi=(pi/180)(30/(NLAT-1)) halve together (true refinement ratio 2). u* is boundary-supercompatible with the zero-flux Neumann band edges (derivations in the problem file), so the recorded relative-L2 / Linf errors are pure O(h^2) truncation drift -- both the cos(lat)-weighted zonal (1/cos^2 phi) and mimetic meridional terms active.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

python._doc: Tight LSODA so the Python temporal truncation is negligible against the spatial goldens on the stiff metric-diffusion sweep.

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Rust hangs at every tolerance tried (loosest reltol 1e-6; all three solvers Erk/Bdf/Sdirk wedge). earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this stiff / non-smooth-min-max / large-AST RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard.
